# PLAN — iteration 3
## Current state assessment
The 7-LUT incumbent is already timing-feasible (WNS 0.553 ns, WHS 0.135 ns), so this iteration must strictly reduce LUT use to improve the `minimize_luts` objective. Iteration 1’s monolithic 8-bit wrapping counter used 10 LUTs, and iteration 2’s comparator rewrite stayed at 7; neither justifies repeating those changes. The top’s numeric latency is unknown, so no numeric annotation is required.

## Hypothesis
Splitting the modulo-256 counter into two 4-bit nibbles, with the upper nibble incrementing only when the lower nibble rolls over, may reduce LUT use by making the rollover and increment logic map more efficiently.

## Instruction for generator
Replace the monolithic counter update with registered low and high 4-bit counters: reset both to zero, increment the low nibble each active cycle, and increment the high nibble when the old low nibble is `4'hF`, allowing both nibbles to wrap naturally. Drive the existing registered PWM comparison from the concatenated nibbles and preserve its reset priority and use of the pre-update count. This differs from iteration 1’s monolithic 8-bit counter; retain the candidate only if unchanged deterministic gates pass, routed setup and hold slack are nonnegative, and routed LUT use is strictly below 7.
